The drawing is a fragment with three wavy-line attachment points, so the SMILES carries three * atoms.

**Triazine ring.** It is a 1,3,5-triazine with three substituents: an NH2 at the top, an HN at the lower left, and an NH–CH2 at the lower right.

**Left attachment.** The lower-left HN is bonded to a carbon (the line to the left) that carries a wavy line crossing it. The bond runs from the left and meets a wavy line that crosses at a vertical bond. It therefore looks like a carbon with two wavy bonds, one going up and one going down, with the horizontal line extending to the left. The picture shows a horizontal line from the far left to the wavy-crossed point, with HN to the right of it. The wavy line crosses the bond that extends up and down from the junction, so the HN is attached to a node that has the wavy line. The simplest reading is that the HN carbon is a quaternary-type junction, with the left stub as a methyl and two wavy bonds, one up and one down.

I read this as N–C(*)(C)… with a wavy bond. Taking the left stub as a plain line, the attached atom is the carbon at the line's end, bearing the left stub (methyl), the up wavy bond and the down wavy bond. That makes it C(C)(*)(*) attached to N.

**Right attachment.** NH–CH2 is attached to a carbon with a wavy line crossing, with one stub going up and a wavy line going lower-left and lower-right. This is a carbon with an up stub (methyl), two wavy bonds and the CH2: CH2–C(C)(*)(*).

**Chain.** Triazine–NH–CH2–NH–C(=O)–NH–CH2–C(C)(*)*.

**SMILES assembly:**
- Left part: *C(C)(*)Nc1nc(N)nc(NCNC(=O)NCC(C)(*)*)n1
- This gives four * atoms, but the image shows only three wavy lines on the left carbon (one crossing, as drawn) plus two on the right.

On the left the wavy line crosses a vertical bond, which appears to be one wavy line. The left horizontal line ends at the junction, and there is one wavy line (vertical, up and down). That is a single wavy bond crossing the carbon, so the left node is a carbon bonded to the left stub, with the wavy line marking the attachment point. I read it as a single attachment on a line, giving N–*. The right side has a wavy line crossing the bond between the upper stub and the lower-right stub, so it is one attachment.

The right attachment is then NH–CH2–C(*)... with a stub up and a wavy line to the lower right. Reading it as one attachment on a carbon with a plain stub and one wavy line gives CH2–C(*)(C), a carbon with a methyl and one attachment. This is a guess, so I settle on the simpler reading with one * per wavy line, three in total.

SMILES: *Nc1nc(N)nc(NCNC(=O)NCC(*)*)n1
